description.narrative:
From February 2020, Kenya National Bureau of Statistics adopted the use of the Washington Group Methodology in the analysis of the 2019 Kenya Housing and Population Census and its upcoming Kenya National Survey for Persons with Disability Facilitated the capacity building of statisticians from the Bureau on the use of the Washington Group Methodology in the analysis of the 2019 Kenya Population and Housing Census(February 2020, 20 officials)
Facilitated the launch and training of the Disability Statistics Technical Working Committee(October 2020, 50 officials from government, NGOs and OPDs)
Supported the production of the Disability Monograph of the 2019 Census(December 2020)
Supported the validation of the Disability Monograph by the Disability Statistics Technical Working Committee and compilation of indicators for the Kenya National Persons with Disabilities Household Survey( February 2021)
Facilitated the development of the Kenya National Survey for Persons with Disabilities Survey instruments(presently)

description.narrative:
The Federation of Kenya Employers (FKE) in 2020 the Kenya Business and Disability Network (KBDN) as an employer-led platform to promote disability inclusion in the workplace.
The Federation of Kenya Employers is operationalizing its gender-responsive, disability inclusion employer engagement strategy
The Federation of Kenya operationalized measures to enhance HIV awareness and testing amongst 48 people with disability in partnership with the Association of Physically Disable Persons in Kenya and LVCT Health in order to enhance disability inclusive HIV response.
The Federation of Kenya Employers and the Central Organization of Trade Unions and its affiliate the Kenya Long Distance and Truck Drivers Union operationalized measures through the VCT@WORK initiative to increase the uptake of HIV services for men in male dominated sectors to include in the transport and agricultural sectors and for informal economy workers reaching over 10,000 workers (updated figures to be provided by 2nd December) 60% of whom were male. The initiatives also increased uptake of HIV self testing through HIV awareness raising, distribution of 3,000 (update figures by 2nd December) while integrating COVID-19 prevention awareness and mitigation measures to include messaging on stigma reduction.(6.4.1)
To mitigate the social economic impact of COVID-19, Women Fighting AIDS in Kenya operationalized measures to enhance economic empowerment of women living and affected by HIV and developed a HIV Sensitive Social Protection Advocacy Brief. Two hundred women have been trained on business skills, linked to financial services providers and provided with start-up seed funds in Kilifi, Homabay and Nairobi. 1. ILO support for establishment of the Kenya Business and Disability Network, included: Support for the formulation of the KBDN strategy for the Federation of Kenya Employers (August 2020); Training of federation staff on disability inclusion (September 2020),-Facilitating and supporting the creation of the Kenya Business and Disability website (November 2020); Support for the launch of the network (including live media coverage) during the Employers' Annual Conference in Nov 2020.
2. In support of operationalization of FKE's employer engagement strategy on gender-responsive disability inclusion, ILO key support is/was on: Supporting the sensitization of private sector employers on disability inclusion(95 in Dec. 2020 and an additional 45 between Jan-March 2021) and on violence and harassment in the workplace(Dec. 2020); Supporting monthly meetings of the Network Supporting the development of guides and publications for the Network; developing a sustainability strategy.
3. To support FKE to operationalize measures for disability inclusive HIV response the ILO sensitized people living with disability on HIV and facilitated LVCT Health disability inclusive counsellors to provide HIV testing and create linkages for care.
4. To support the roll out of the VCT@WORK initiative targeting male dominated sectors, trained 40 male champions on HIV, GBV and gender equality and facilitated the mobilization of formal and informal workplaces for HIV awareness and testing; supported partnership building with county governments of Kilifi and Makueni for provision of testing commodities and mobilization of counsellors. Facilitated provision of COVID-19 awareness materials, masks and sanitizers
5. Contributed to the economic empowerment of women living and affected by HIV through building their capacity on business skills, provision of business start-up seed funds and proving technical inputs to the HIV sensitive social protection advocacy brief.
